I selected the materials for a suit, with the assistance of Mr. Trabb's judgment,
and re-entered the parlor to be measured.
For although Mr. Trabb had my measure already, and had previously been quite contented with
it, he said apologetically that it wouldn't do under existing circumstances, sir, wouldn't
do at all.
So Mr. Trabb measured and calculated me in the parlor, as if I were in a state and he
the finest species of surveyor, and gave himself such a world of trouble that I felt that
no suit of clothes could possibly remunerate him for his pains.
When he had it last done, and had appointed to send the articles to Mr. Pumblechook, S.
on the Thursday evening, he said, with his hand upon the parlor lock, I know, sir, that
London gentlemen cannot be expected to patronize local work as a rule, but if you would give
me a turn now and then in the quality of a townsman, I should greatly esteem it.
Good morning, sir, much obliged.
Door.
